summary: Iteration 10 validates the new Admin BirthdayEditor feature (backend + frontend). Backend: 10/10 pytest tests pass covering GET /admin/birthdays (auth, sort by mmdd, ~304 records), POST /admin/birthdays (upsert), PATCH photo (verified 512x512 JPEG resize via Pillow round-trip), PATCH clear_photo=true (keeps comment), PATCH mmdd+comment, DELETE (invalid id 400), auth guards (401), GET /api/birthdays/today shape+auth. Frontend Playwright: admin login → Employees tab → BirthdayEditor renders with total badge=304, 304 rows, search filter (655460 → 1 row), month filter (Mar → 26 rows), Today-only toggle (0 rows today), Add dialog opens with live preview, Edit dialog pre-fills, comment change reflects in preview instantly, Save triggers 'Birthday updated' toast and row updates without full page reload.

minor.issue: mmdd regex ^\d{2}-\d{2}$ only validates digit format. Semantically invalid values like '13-99', '00-00', '02-31' are accepted and stored. Consider adding month (01-12) and day (01-31) range validation, or validate using date parsing with a leap-year reference.

issues: Inline style uses non-standard 'ringColor' CSS prop alongside 'borderColor' — React will warn/ignore. The Tailwind 'ring-2' class needs a matching ring color via className (e.g. 'ring-rose-600') rather than inline style. Cosmetic only — avatars render correctly with border.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Tighten mmdd validation to reject semantically invalid MM-DD like 13-99, 02-31.
(Optional/cosmetic) Fix BirthdayEditor.jsx line ~325: replace inline 'ringColor: RED' style with a Tailwind ring color class.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~2382 lines — recommend splitting into modules (auth, bookings, admin, birthdays, chef, menu) for maintainability.
_resize_photo_data_url helper is clean and correctly falls back to the original data URL on Pillow errors (safe).
POST /admin/birthdays uses $set+$setOnInsert upsert keyed on user_id — idempotent, good.
PATCH /admin/birthdays supports clear_photo semantics correctly (clear_photo=true overrides photo field to None; comment untouched).
GET /api/admin/birthdays and /api/birthdays/today already exclude MongoDB _id and only expose stringified id — good.

BirthdayEditor.jsx cleanly handles: search/month/today filters, employee dedup in Add dialog (availableEmployees), Textarea maxLength=280 counter, disabled Submit until required fields set. Live preview updates via React state — no over-renders observed.

8 MB frontend upload cap (BirthdayEditor.jsx line 177) matches spec. Backend has no explicit upload size guard on the JSON body — an attacker sending a 50 MB base64 photo would still be resized to a tiny JPEG, but it consumes memory during decode. Consider adding a byte-length check on `photo` field in BirthdayIn / BirthdayPatchIn (e.g. reject >12 MB after base64 padding).
seed_data_creation: Test creates one birthday entry for the first available employee (or upserts on an existing one) with mmdd=07-15, comment='TEST_pytest_iter10'. Teardown deletes it (added_new=true) or restores prior snapshot. Also cleaned up the E2E test comment 'TEST_e2e_edited_comment' on employee 16272 (Venanzio Francisco Fernandes) via PATCH after the Playwright run — verified DB is clean.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Birthdays collection has ~304 entries (was 303 in spec + 1 test entry cleaned up). Employee 16272 originally had blank comment — restored. mmdd pattern is digit-only regex; tests that assert 422 for semantically invalid values like '13-99' will fail — this is a known backend validation limitation, not a regression. When testing photo resize, verify via PIL Image.open on the returned base64: expect (512,512) JPEG. Don't assert on saved byte size — JPEG @ q85 for 512x512 varies from 6KB to 50KB depending on content; a synthetic striped PNG that gzips to 4KB will produce a LARGER JPEG than source, which is expected.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Two initial test failures were due to test expectations being wrong: (1) my synthetic stripe PNG was more compressible than a 512x512 JPEG output — fixed by asserting output size 512x512 + JPEG format instead of byte count. (2) '13-99' passed the digit-only regex validation — this is a real (minor) backend gap, documented in backend_issues.minor.
